scope: Boat-based recreational starting methods. Regional rules, closed areas, sea state and species identification are checked separately for the selected trip.

reef.priority: Sound a measured reef edge, then make short controlled bottom passes rather than drifting blindly across the whole polygon.
find: Rock relief adjoining sand or a ledge; note bait and marks both on and above the bottom.
Choose a pass with room to set up upwind or up-current and safely clear the reef.
reef.rig: Start with one rod and a two-hook dropper-loop rig with bait or soft plastics and enough weight to maintain intermittent bottom contact. A single heavy swimbait or jig is another lingcod option. Carry a ready descending device.
steps: Idle over the feature and mark the high point, edge, and fish depth on the sounder.
Make a short test drift across the edge; lower to the actual marks and lift clear of snags.
Repeat productive passes and reset when line angle or bottom contact deteriorates.
reef.adjust: If marks are suspended, fish their depth instead of dragging bottom. Identify every rockfish before retention; a reef grade does not identify species.

variants.name: Lingcod
variants.focus: Ledges, rough edges and bottom-adjacent marks.
variants.presentation: A large single swimbait/jig or bait close to bottom; make controlled passes along relief.

variants.name: Rockfish
variants.focus: Identify bottom and suspended marks, then fish at the marked depth.
variants.presentation: A lawful two-hook dropper rig with bait or soft plastics is a starting setup; keep the descending device ready.

pacific-halibut.priority: Search a legal northern continental-shelf bottom lane with a controlled near-bottom presentation; verify bait and drift on the boat.
find: Surveyed shelf sediment or mixed-bottom edges with a manageable drift and room to reset safely.
A local depth band supported by actual bottom data, not a fixed statewide halibut depth or an unverified California-halibut pin.
pacific-halibut.rig: One line with no more than two hooks when angling for Pacific halibut. A baited near-bottom rig or a single jig can be a starting presentation; set weight by actual line angle and current. Check the current quota and local season before leaving.
steps: Confirm the Pacific halibut season and any quota closure, exact MPA and bottom-access rules for the trip date.
Sound a legal shelf lane, note bottom, bait and boat drift, then make a short near-bottom test pass.
Record effort and empty drifts; change depth or lane only when conditions and observed evidence support the move.
pacific-halibut.adjust: Adult fish can feed away from bottom and move seasonally across the shelf. A soft-bottom polygon or a temperature edge does not establish current presence; improve boat control or search another verified lane.

halibut.priority: Test soft-bottom lanes adjoining bait or habitat edges with a slow, controlled near-bottom presentation.
find: Sand, mud, or surfgrass margin with bait and a clear lane for a repeatable drift.
Depth and bottom changes on the sounder; one sediment polygon is only a broad search window.
halibut.rig: A live-bait sliding-sinker or leader rig, or a single swimbait/jighead, is a practical start. Keep bait or lure near bottom while avoiding a sinker that plows continuously.
steps: Sound the lane for bait and a change in bottom or depth.
Make a short drift or controlled slow pass with the presentation just off bottom.
Repeat or shift lanes only after recording the pass and whether bottom contact and bait were present.
halibut.adjust: If the rig rides high, change weight or drift angle. If it drags, lighten or raise it. Do not infer fish presence from soft sediment alone.

salmon.priority: Only during an open fishery, search bait and salmon marks in the water column and troll at the observed depth.
find: Fresh forage and fish marks, not a reef grade or old landing report.
Legal season and transit route for the chosen area, plus a full return-weather window.
salmon.rig: Use a lawful trolling presentation with the required barbless single-point hooks and one rod per angler north of Point Conception. Bait-fishing hook rules differ by area and method; verify the current CDFW card before rigging.
steps: Check today's salmon opening, subarea, possession and hook rules.
Sound for bait and fish depth, then set trolling depth to those marks.
Make repeatable passes and record empty effort as well as hookups.
salmon.adjust: If bait is absent or fish depth changes, change water or depth. Never deploy salmon gear while transiting a closed area with salmon aboard.

method_sources.title: CDFW ocean salmon regulations and gear

dungeness.priority: Test multiple lawful soft-bottom depths with equal bait and soak effort instead of assuming deeper water beats sea-otter predation.
find: Verified sand/mud bottom with safe line length, traffic separation and lawful gear access.
A depth comparison that records empty sets, bait, soak time and sea-otter interactions.
dungeness.rig: Use a compliant baited hoop net or, only where currently allowed, a crab trap with required validation, escape/biodegradable features and buoy marking. Size line, buoy and retrieval equipment for the actual depth and conditions.
steps: Check the season, current whale-entanglement gear restrictions and local MPAs.
Set comparable gear in a few depth bands, recording soak time and location precision.
Retrieve safely, measure crabs, and log both catches and zero sets.
dungeness.adjust: If shallow sets fail, compare a qualified deeper band rather than jumping straight to 300 feet. No universal depth optimum or local otter-effect threshold is established.

albacore.priority: Search current offshore water boundaries with a controlled troll and confirm feeding activity before concentrating effort.
find: Fresh SST/current transition with bait, birds, fish marks or recent dated catch evidence.
Fuel reserve and a safe return window for the whole offshore route.
albacore.rig: Use a small trolling-lure spread to cover water; have a bait or casting setup ready if fish are located. Match tackle and lure depth to observed fish and conditions.
steps: Compare both sides of a recent water transition.
Run repeatable search legs while recording temperature, bait and empty passes.
When fish are confirmed, work that water mass and reassess after activity stops.
albacore.adjust: If imagery is clouded, stale or fish signs are absent, lower confidence and expand or end the search; no universal temperature cutoff is used.

limitations: Starter boat-fishing methods only. Check date- and position-specific rules, gear, MPA access, species ID, conditions, and actual fish/forage signs before fishing.
